DAMGHANI:v1p450/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p450/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p450/r1.claim: Nidāʾ can mean supplication; al-Anbiyāʾ gives further examples.
DAMGHANI:v1p450/r1.anchor: النداء الدعاء قوله سبحانه في سورة مريم

BURSEVI:v5p240#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p240#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p240#2/r6.claim: Zakariyya prayed quietly in the Jerusalem sanctuary after making an offering; secrecy showed good manners, sincerity, and freedom from show, hid his request from hostile relatives, and spared him public censure over seeking a child in old age.
BURSEVI:v5p240#2/r6.anchor: ولقد راعى عليه السلام حسن الأدب في دعائه فإنه مع كونه بالنسبة إليه تعالى كالجهر أدخل في الإخلاص

ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r1.claim: Idh may modify raḥma or dhikr, or be an appositive of inclusion to Zakariya, as in the passage about Maryam withdrawing to an eastern place.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r1.anchor: هو بدل اشتمال من ( زكريا ) كما قوله تعالى ( واذكر في الكتاب مريم إذ انتبذت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r2.speaker: الحسن وابن يعمر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r2.claim: They read dhakkara as an intensified past verb and raḥmata in the accusative; its first object is omitted, its second is mercy, and ʿabdahu is the object of mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r2.anchor: قرأ الحسن وابن يعمر كما حكاه أبو الفتح ( ذكر ) فعلا ماضيا مشددا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r3.speaker: أبو الفتح
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r3.claim: The subject of dhakkara may be the Quran from context, the disjoint letters construed as Quran, or God; people are the omitted object.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r3.anchor: وفاعل ( ذكر ) ضمير القرآن المعلوم من السياق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r4.claim: Other parses make mercy the second object and ʿabdahu the first, or mercy the first and ʿabdahu the second; another takes the phrase metaphorically as God making mercy remember His servant.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ( رحمة ربك ) مفعولا ثانيا والمفعول الأول هو ( عبده )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r5.speaker: أبو يعمر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r5.claim: Al-Dani reports Abu Yaʿmar reading an imperative: remind people of your Lord’s mercy toward Zakariya, directly or by means of that mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p58#2/r5.anchor: وذكر الداني عن أبي يعمر أنه قرأ ( ذكر ) على الأمر والتشديد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi reads dhakara as a light past verb, raḥmata as its object, and ʿabdahu as its subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r1.anchor: وقرأ الكلبي ( ذكر ) فعلا ماضيا خفيفا و ( رحمة ربك ) بالنصب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r2.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Zakariya was the last prophet of the Children of Israel.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r2.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وصححه عن ابن مسعود أنه آخر أنبياء بني إسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Zakariya was the son of Dan and one of the prophetic descendants who wrote revelation in Jerusalem.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن إسحاق بن بشر وابن عساكر عن ابن عباس أنه ابن دان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r4.claim: A sound-graded report from Abu Hurayra says Zakariya was a carpenter.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا أنه عليه السلام كان نجارا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r5.claim: Zakariya’s name has five forms: long and short forms read in the Seven, two forms of Zakari, and Zakar like qalam; it is foreign.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r5.anchor: وجاء في اسمه خمس لغات تولها المد وثانيها القصر وقريء بهما في السبع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r6.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r6.claim: Nidāʾ ordinarily means raising and projecting the voice, but Raghib allows it to mean any sound or any sign indicating something.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r6.anchor: وقد يقال لمجرد الصوت بل لكل ما يدل على شيء وإن لم يكن صوتا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r7.claim: Here nidāʾ means supplication privately made and unheard by people, perhaps in the middle of the night; secrecy better protects sincerity and avoids ostentation, reproach, and harm from his relatives.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r7.anchor: مستورا عن الناس لم يسمعه أحد منهم حيث لم يكونوا حاضريه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r8.claim: Secrecy need not mean a quiet voice: he could call loudly where nobody could see or hear him; alternatively hiddenness is a figure for sincerity and lack of ostentation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r8.anchor: ومن رفع صوته في مكان ليس بمرأى ولا مسمع من الناس فقد أخفاه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r9.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r9.claim: Al-Kashf regards the phrase as a figure with literal secrecy also intended: concealment itself was desired, while sincerity was the chief purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59/r9.anchor: وفي الكشف أن الأشبه أنه كناية مع إرادة الحقيقة لأن الخفاء في نفسه مطلوب أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p59#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59#2/r1.claim: His call may have been hidden because his voice weakened with age, as a saying describes an old person’s voice as faint and hearing as intermittent.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59#2/r1.anchor: لضعف صوته بسبب كبره كما قيل الشيخ صوته خفات وسمعه تارات

ALUSI-FULL:v16p59#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59#2/r2.claim: Reported ages range from sixty to 120 years; 120 best fits the explanation that age weakened his voice.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p59#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : كان سنه حينئذ ستين سنة وقيل خمسا وستين وقيل سبعين وقيل خمسا وسبعين وقيل ثمانين وقيل خمسا وثمانين وقيل اثنتين وتسعين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p218/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p218/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p218/r1.claim: Zachariah prayed to his Lord in his prayer chamber, secretly during the night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p218/r1.anchor: {إذ نادى} دعا {ربه} في محرابه {نداء خفيا} دعا سرا من قومه في جوف الليل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:3/r1.claim: Zachariah prayed quietly because concealment deepens humility and sincerity, lest he be criticized for seeking a child in old age, lest his dependents hear, or because age weakened his voice.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:3/r1.anchor: لأن الإخفاء والجهر عند الله سيان

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:3/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:3/r2.claim: Reports differ about Zachariah's age at the time: sixty, seventy, seventy-five, eighty-five, or ninety-nine.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:3/r2.anchor: واختلف في سنه حينئذ فقيل ستون

BIQAI-FULL:v4p519/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p519/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p519/r5.claim: His hidden prayer suits the intimacy of a close lover's private address to the beloved; God nevertheless knows even the most secret plea.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p519/r5.anchor: كما يفعل المحب القريب مع حبيبه المقبل عليه في قصد خطاب السر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p519/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p519/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p519/r6.claim: Calling God simply Lord without a vocative particle signals extreme closeness.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p519/r6.anchor: { قال رب } بحذف الأداة للدلالة على غاية القرب

DURR-FULL:v5p479/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p479/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p479/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Zakariya as son of Dan, father of Yahya, and a prophetic descendant who wrote revelation in Jerusalem's sanctuary.
DURR-FULL:v5p479/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن زكريا بن دان أبا يحيى كان من أبناء الأنبياء

DURR-FULL:v5p479/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p479/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v5p479/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Zakariya prayed quietly to avoid showing off.
DURR-FULL:v5p479/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا} قال: لا يريد رياء

DURR-FULL:v5p479/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p479/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p479/r3.claim: Qatada says the quiet call was a secret prayer in the heart and that God loves a soft voice and pure heart.
DURR-FULL:v5p479/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا} أي بقلبه سرا قال قتادة: إن الله يحب الصوت الخفي

QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r10.claim: Private supplication has merit beyond public calling; Abraham's story combines calling at the start with intimate address later, with God caring for him throughout.
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r10.anchor: للنجوى مزية على النداء ، فجمع له الوصفين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r7.claim: Nidaʾ means supplication and earnest request.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Zachariah prayed privately because hidden acts are better and farther from ostentation, citing the report that the best remembrance is private.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r8.anchor: فقال ابن جريج ذلك لأن الأعمال الخفية أفضل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r9.claim: Another view says worship that purifies a person should be private between servant and Lord; hiding a prayer for forgiveness also avoids ostentation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r9.anchor: وقال غيره يستحب الإخفاء بين العبد ومولاه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r10.claim: Because Zachariah sought a child, one explanation says he hid the worldly request to avoid blame if it went unanswered; another says he prayed in the middle of the night.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p4/r10.anchor: وأما دعاء زكريا وطلبه فكان في أمر دنياوي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r2.claim: Zakariya concealed his prayer to avoid ostentation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r2.anchor: أحدها ليبعد عن الرياء قاله ابن جريج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r3.claim: He prayed quietly so people would not mock an old man asking for a child in old age.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r3.anchor: لئلا يقول الناس انظروا إلى هذا الشيخ يسأل الولد على الكبر قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r4.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r4.claim: He feared his cousins would resent him and think he opposed their succeeding him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r4.anchor: لئلا يعاديه بنو عمه ويظنوا أنه كره أن يلوا مكانه بعده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r5.claim: The story supports the recommendation to make supplication privately, as in the hadith that people are not calling on a deaf one.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p206#3/r5.anchor: وهذه القصة تدل على أن المستحب إسرار الدعاء ومنه الحديث إنكم لا تدعون أصم

SULAMI:v1p420#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p420#4/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p420#4/r1.claim: Zakariyya concealed his call from people and even from himself, making it manifest only to the One who answers and can grant it, so that spiritual fluctuation would not enter it.
SULAMI:v1p420#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أخفى نداءه عن الخلق وعن نفسه ، وأظهر النداء لمن يجيبه ويقدر على إجابته

SULAMI:v1p420#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p420#4/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p420#4/r2.claim: The call was hidden within remembrance, away from remembrance; when divine majesty overwhelms a person, the heart and tongue fall silent from invoking.
SULAMI:v1p420#4/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم في قوله : ﴿ إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا ﴾ . قال : خفيا في الذكرعن الذكر ،

SULAMI:v1p420#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p420#4/r3.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p420#4/r3.claim: True remembrance is a state in which the rememberer is subsumed.
SULAMI:v1p420#4/r3.anchor: وقيل : حقيقة الذكر ما يندرج فيه الذاكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r1.claim: The disconnected letters were discussed at the beginning of al-Baqara; this passage calls the account God's mercy to Zakariya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {ذكر رحمة ربك} أي: هذا ذكر رحمة الله بعبده زكريا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r2.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r2.claim: He reads the phrase with Zakariya in the accusative construction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر "ذكر رحمة ربك عبده زكريا".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r3.claim: Zakariya is a great Israelite prophet; his name has two well-known readings, lengthened and shortened, and Sahih al-Bukhari says he worked as a carpenter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r3.anchor: {زكريا} : يمد ويقصر قراءتان مشهورتان. وكان نبيا عظيما من أنبياء بني إسرائيل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r4.speaker: الماوردي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r4.claim: One explanation says Zakariya hid the prayer lest people call his request for a child in old age rashness; al-Mawardi transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r4.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين: إنما أخفى دعاءه، لئلا ينسب في طلب الولد إلى الرعونة لكبره. حكاه الماوردي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r5.claim: Another explanation says hidden prayer is more beloved to God; Qatada says God knows the pious heart and hears a quiet voice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r5.anchor: كما قال قتادة في هذه الآية {إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا} : إن الله يعلم القلب التقي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r6.speaker: بعض السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r6.claim: An early report pictures Zakariya praying at night after companions slept, softly repeating Lord, and God answering him three times.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p211#2/r6.anchor: قام من الليل، عليه السلام، وقد نام أصحابه، فجعل يهتف بربه يقول خفية: يا رب،

JISHUMI:v6p4514/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4514/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4514/r10.claim: Nidāʾan is a direct object and khafiyyan describes it.
JISHUMI:v6p4514/r10.anchor: ندآء) نصب لأنه مفعول. (خفيا) نعت له

JISHUMI:v6p4519/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4519/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4519/r5.claim: The best supplication is quiet; a Prophetic report praises hidden remembrance and sufficient provision, which better avoids showing off.
JISHUMI:v6p4519/r5.anchor: ويدل قوله: (نداء خفيا) أن أفضل الدعاء ما هذا حاله، وروي: خير الذكر الخفي، وخير الرزق ما يكفي

JISHUMI:v6p4519/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4519/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4519/r6.claim: At the start of supplication it is recommended to recall God's blessings and to plead humbly.
JISHUMI:v6p4519/r6.anchor: ويدل ما قال على أن المستحب في مقدمة الدعاء ذكر نعمه، والتضرع، والخضوع

AKHFASH:v2p437/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p437/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p437/r2.claim: خفيا is formed from the notion of concealment, from الإخفاء.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r6.claim: Zakariya follows God's practice of concealing supplication; concealment is preferable because public and private speech are equal before God, while privacy is farther from ostentation and more sincere.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r6.anchor: راعى سنة الله في إخفاء دعوته ، لأن الجهر والإخفاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r7.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r7.claim: Al-Hasan explains the hidden call as a prayer without ostentation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r7.anchor: وعن الحسن نداء لا رياء فيه ، أو أخفاه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r8.claim: One explanation is that Zakariya hid his request to avoid blame for asking for a child in old age.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r8.anchor: أو أخفاه لئلا يلام على طلب الولد في إبان الكبرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r9.claim: Another explanation is that he kept the prayer from the relatives whose conduct he feared.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r9.anchor: أو أسره من مواليه الذين خافهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r10.claim: A further explanation is that his voice was weak from frailty and old age.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r10.anchor: أو خفت صوته لضعفه وهرمه ، كما جاء في صفة الشيخ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r11.claim: Reported estimates of Zakariya's age are sixty, sixty-five, seventy, seventy-five, and eighty-five.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p5/r11.anchor: واختلف في سن زكريا عليه السلام ، فقيل : ستون ، وخمس وستون

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r25.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r25.anchor: أحدهما : قاله ابن جريج , سرا لا رياء فيه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r26.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r26.claim: God knows a pure heart and hears a quiet voice; Zakariya kept the call quiet to avoid being accused of ostentation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r26.anchor: قال قتادة إن الله يعلم القلب النقي ويسمع الصوت الخفي فأخفى زكريا نداءه لئلا ينسب إلى الرياء فيه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r27.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r27.claim: Zakariya hid his prayer so people would not mock an old man asking for a child.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r27.anchor: الثاني : قاله مقاتل , إنما أخفى لئلا يهزأ الناس به , فيقولون انظروا إلى هذا الشيخ يسأل الولد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r28.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r28.claim: A hidden prayer may be more sincere and more likely to be answered, in keeping with the teaching that the one invoked is not deaf.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p352#2/r28.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : أن إخفاء الدعاء أخلص للدعاء وأرجى للإجابة للسنة الواردة فيه : إن الذي تدعونه ليس بأصم .

MUQATIL:19:2-5/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:2-5/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:2-5/r2.claim: Zakariya prayed secretly so people would not remark that an old man was asking for a child in old age.
MUQATIL:19:2-5/r2.anchor: لئلا يقول الناس: انظروا إلى هذا الشيخ الكبير، يسأل الولد على كبره.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p30#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p30#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p30#3/r1.claim: Idh is an adverb attached to raḥmah.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p30#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p30#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p30#3/r2.claim: Secret prayer follows the command and avoids ostentation, drawing the worshipper nearer to purity.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p30#3/r2.anchor: دعاه دعاء سرا كما هو المأمور به وهو أبعد عن الرياء وأقرب إلى الصفاء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p30#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p30#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p30#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, Zechariah hid his prayer so he would not be blamed for asking for a child in old age; he was seventy-five or eighty.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p30#3/r3.anchor: أو أخفاه لئلا يلام على طلب الولد في أوان الكبر لأنه كان ابن خمس وسبعين أو ثمانين سنة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:2-3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:2-3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:2-3/r8.claim: Nida' is supplication and longing; Zechariah privately addressed God in his prayer chamber, as shown by the account of the angels calling him while he prayed.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:2-3/r8.anchor: والنداء الدعاء والرغبة أي ناجى ربه بذلك في محرابه

QURTUBI-FULL:19:2-3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:2-3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:2-3/r9.claim: Possible reasons for hiding the prayer include avoiding blame, sincerity, avoiding ostentation, or praying secretly at night; al-Qurtubi says the first is clearest, while secrecy in supplication is commendable.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:2-3/r9.anchor: واختلف في إخفائه هذا النداء فقيل: أخفاه من قومه لئلا يلام

QURTUBI-FULL:19:2-3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:2-3/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:19:2-3/r10.claim: A report from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas says the best remembrance is hidden and the best provision is what suffices.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:2-3/r10.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:19:3-5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:3-5/r1.speaker: يونس بن عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:19:3-5/r1.claim: Yunus says al-Hasan favored silent qunut by the imam and silent amens from those behind, citing Zechariah's hidden prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:3-5/r1.anchor: قال يونس بن عبيد: كان الحسن يرى أن يدعو الإمام في القنوت

QURTUBI-FULL:19:3-5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:3-5/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:3-5/r2.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says Malik made qunut quiet and al-Shafi'i loud; loudness is preferable because the Prophet prayed it aloud.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:3-5/r2.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وقد أسر مالك القنوت وجهر به الشافعي،

RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r1.claim: Zakariyyā hid his call in keeping with God's practice: secrecy avoids show and better expresses sincerity, although loud and quiet calls are equal before God.
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r1.anchor: لأن الجهر والإخفاء عند الله سيان فكان الإخفاء أولى لأنه أبعد عن الرياء

RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r2.claim: One explanation says he concealed the request lest people blame him for seeking a child in old age.
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r2.anchor: أخفاه لئلا يلام على طلب الولد في زمان الشيخوخة

RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r3.claim: Another explanation says he kept it from the relatives whose conduct he feared.

RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r4.claim: A further explanation attributes the quiet voice to his weakness and advanced age.

RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r5.claim: The call can be both a nidāʾ and quiet: he raised his voice as much as he could, but age made it faint, so intention made it a call and reality made it quiet.
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r5.anchor: فكان نداء نظرا إلى قصده وخفيا نظرا إلى الواقع

RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, he prayed during the ritual prayer, since the angels answered while he stood praying in the sanctuary; supplication in prayer would be quiet.
RAZI-FULL:v21p153#2/r6.anchor: فنادته الملئكة وهو قائم يصلى فى المحراب

RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r9.claim: The first lesson in the story is etiquette in supplication: the quiet call shows that the best prayer is humble, concealed, and reliant on God's grace rather than one's own strength, as 7:55 teaches.
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r9.anchor: وهو يدل على أن أفضل الدعاء ما هذا حاله

RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r10.claim: Raising the voice suggests strength and firmness, while lowering it conveys weakness and surrender, the proper posture of supplication.
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r10.anchor: رفع الصوت مشعر بالقوة والجلادة وإخفاء الصوت مشعر بالضعف والانكسار

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r4.claim: Zachariah’s secret supplication signals sincerity; loud prayer can suggest hypocrisy or seeking human notice.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r4.anchor: That Zachariah cries out to God with a secret cry indicates his sincerity

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r5.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r5.claim: A low voice is especially favored by God.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r5.anchor: this mode of supplication is particularly favored by God (IK)

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r6.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r6.claim: Zachariah may have prayed quietly because of age and frailty or fear of his relatives.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r6.anchor: as a result of his age and frailty (Z), or because of fear of his relatives

NAHHAS:v3p5/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p5/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p5/r2.claim: إذ is temporal and accusative; نداء is an emphatic verbal noun and خفيا describes it.
NAHHAS:v3p5/r2.anchor: في موضع نصب على الظرف ( نادى ربه نداء ) مصدر مؤكد

TAB-FULL:v15p452/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p452/r1.speaker: نحوي بصري
TAB-FULL:v15p452/r1.claim: A Basran grammarian supplies 'among what is recited to you' and makes ʿabd the object of raḥma.
TAB-FULL:v15p452/r1.anchor: فقال بعض نحويي البصرة في معنى ذلك كأنه قال: مما نقص عليك ذكر رحمة ربك عبده

TAB-FULL:v15p452/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p452/r2.speaker: نحوي كوفي
TAB-FULL:v15p452/r2.claim: A Kufan grammarian makes dhikr governed by the opening letters, or supplies 'this is the mention of your Lord's mercy,' with reordered wording.
TAB-FULL:v15p452/r2.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: رفعت الذكر بكهيعص، وإن شئت أضمرت هذا ذكر رحمة ربك

TAB-FULL:v15p452/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p452/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p452/r3.claim: He prefers an omitted demonstrative subject, 'this is the mention'; ʿabd is accusative after raḥma and Zakariyyā explains it in apposition.
TAB-FULL:v15p452/r3.anchor: الذكر مرفوع بمضمر محذوف وهو هذا، كما فعل ذلك في غيرها من السور

TAB-FULL:v15p454/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p454/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p454/r1.claim: Zakariyyā prayed secretly to avoid ostentation.
TAB-FULL:v15p454/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا} [مريم: 3] أي سرا، وإن الله يعلم القلب النقي

TAB-FULL:v15p454/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p454/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p454/r2.claim: He glosses the prayer as secret, adding that God knows a pure heart and hears a quiet voice.
TAB-FULL:v15p454/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا} [مريم: 3] أي سرا، وإن الله يعلم القلب النقي

TAB-FULL:v15p454/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p454/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p454/r3.claim: He says Zakariyyā did not want to show off.
TAB-FULL:v15p454/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: {إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا} [مريم: 3] قال: لا يريد رياء

TAB-FULL:v15p454/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p454/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v15p454/r4.claim: He says Zakariyyā wanted a child, prayed privately, and made the request that follows.
TAB-FULL:v15p454/r4.anchor: عن السدي، قال: رغب زكريا في الولد، فقام فصلى، ثم دعا ربه سرا

TABATABAI:19:1-3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-3/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is warning and glad tidings, illustrated through the stories of prophets granted divine friendship, prophethood, truthfulness, and sincerity.
TABATABAI:19:1-3/r1.anchor: هو التبشير والإنذار غير أنه ساق الكلام في ذلك سوقا بديعا

TABATABAI:19:1-3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-3/r2.claim: The surah contrasts humble, grateful predecessors with descendants who abandon devotion for desire and error, while allowing repentant believers to return to the blessed path.
TABATABAI:19:1-3/r2.anchor: لكن أخلافهم أعرضوا عن ذلك وأهملوا أمر التوجه إلى ربهم واتبعوا الشهوات

TABATABAI:19:1-3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-3/r3.claim: Stories serve as examples for a general division into the blessed, the erring, and repentant believers, followed by their respective reward and punishment; the surah rebuts denials of resurrection, divine offspring, and worship of idols.
TABATABAI:19:1-3/r3.anchor: فالسورة تقسم الناس إلى ثلاث طوائف الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين وأهل الإجتباء والهدى

TABATABAI:19:3-8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:3-8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:3-8/r1.claim: The time clause attaches to God’s mercy; nida ordinarily means calling aloud, unlike private supplication, but can be hidden when spoken where people cannot hear.
TABATABAI:19:3-8/r1.anchor: والنداء والمناداة الجهر بالدعوة خلاف المناجاة

TABATABAI:19:3-8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:3-8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:3-8/r2.claim: The description of the call as hidden is compatible with speaking aloud in private, as Zechariah later leaves the prayer niche to address his people.
TABATABAI:19:3-8/r2.anchor: لإمكان الجهر بالدعوة في خلاء من الناس لا يسمعون معه الدعوة

TABATABAI:19:3-8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:3-8/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:19:3-8/r3.claim: Some say Zechariah used the word calling because his sins and poor condition made him feel distant from God, like someone fearing punishment.
TABATABAI:19:3-8/r3.anchor: وقيل إن العناية في التعبير بالنداء أنه تصور نفسه بعيدا منه تعالى بذنوبه

TABATABAI:19:15/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:15/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:15/r7.claim: The Qur'an calls Zechariah prophet and recipient of revelation, servant, righteous, elect, and guided; it recounts his prayer for a child after witnessing Mary's worship and provision.
TABATABAI:19:15/r7.anchor: وصفه الله سبحانه في كلامه بالنبوة والوحي

TABRISI:19:1-6/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:1-6/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:1-6/r8.claim: Prayer is a request for an action from the one invoked, and its counterpart is a response, just as obedience answers a command.
TABRISI:19:1-6/r8.anchor: والدعاء طلب الفعل من المدعو وفي مقابلته الإجابة

TABRISI:19:1-6#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:1-6#3/r1.speaker: الحديث
TABRISI:19:1-6#3/r1.claim: A hadith states that the best prayer is quiet and the best provision is what suffices.
TABRISI:19:1-6#3/r1.anchor: خير الدعاء الخفي وخير الرزق ما يكفي

TABRISI:19:1-6#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:1-6#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:1-6#3/r2.claim: Zakariya may have concealed his prayer to avoid people mocking an elderly man for asking for a child.
TABRISI:19:1-6#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: إنما أخفاه لئلا يهزأ به الناس

THALABI:v6p206/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p206/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p206/r2.claim: Zachariah prayed secretly in his sanctuary at night, where offerings were brought near, sincerely and unseen by anyone but God.
THALABI:v6p206/r2.anchor: إذ نادى دعا ربه في محرابه حيث يقرب القربان نداء خفيا دعاء سرا من قومه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r1.claim: Khafiy means hidden; the adjective may be khāfin or khafī, like sāmiʿ and samīʿ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r1.anchor: بمعنى: الخافي، يقال: خفي الشيء يخفى، خفاء، فهو خاف، وخفي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r2.claim: Zechariah kept the prayer hidden within himself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد يخفي ذلك في نفسه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r3.claim: He prayed quietly to avoid showing off.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Muslims supplicated in near-whispers following 7:55; God praises Zechariah’s quiet prayer, showing that concealment is recommended.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r4.anchor: قال الحسن: (وقد كان المسلمون يجتهدون في الدعاء، وما يسمع لهم صوت إن كان إلا همسا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī says he hid his prayer from his people so they would not hear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (أخفاه وأسره عن قومه لئلا يسمعوه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري عن الكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r6.claim: They say he concealed the prayer out of embarrassment at being an elderly man who still longed for a child and feared criticism.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p187#2/r6.anchor: وهذا القول حكاه ابن الأنباري عن الكلبي، ومقاتل بن سليمان قالا: (إنما أخفى نداءه استيحاء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:1-4/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:1-4/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:1-4/r3.claim: Zechariah's prayer was private, a secret known to no one but God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:1-4/r3.anchor: نداءا خفيا } سرا لم يطلع عليه غير الله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p213/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p213/r4.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p213/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Zakariyya's quiet invocation was a prayer free of ostentation.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p213/r4.anchor: {إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا} [مريم: 3] دعاء لا رياء فيه في تفسير الحسن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p213/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p213/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p213/r5.claim: Qatāda glosses the quiet invocation as secret.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p213/r5.anchor:
وقال قتادة: خفيا، سرا.
حماد، عن ثابت البناني، عن عقبة بن عبد الغافر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p213/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p213/r6.speaker: عقبة بن عبد الغافر
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p213/r6.claim: ʿUqba ibn ʿAbd al-Ghāfir says a private prayer is better than seventy public ones.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p213/r6.anchor: عن عقبة بن عبد الغافر قال: دعوة السر أفضل من سبعين في العلانية.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:2/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:2/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:2/r2.claim: Quiet, humble, pleading prayer best fits its etiquette; Zakariya feared his relatives would fail to lead the community and spread God's religion, so he sought a virtuous, capable, just successor from himself and Jacob's line, never despairing of God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:2/r2.anchor: alçak sesle ve yalvarıp yakararak yapılması onun âdâbına daha uygun olduğu için alçak sesle dua ettiği belirtilen Hz. Zekeriyyâ

SAMIN-DURR:19:3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:3/r1.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:19:3/r1.claim: Al-Ḥawfī gives dhikr as the governor of idh nādā.
SAMIN-DURR:19:3/r1.anchor: قوله: { إذ نادى }: في ناصبه ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أنه " ذكر " ولم يذكر الحوفي غيره

SAMIN-DURR:19:3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:3/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:19:3/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ lists both dhikr and raḥmah as possible governors of idh nādā.
SAMIN-DURR:19:3/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه " رحمة " ، وقد ذكر الوجهين أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:19:3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:3/r3.claim: A third option makes idh nādā an appositive of Zakariyyā by inclusion, since the time contains the event; compare 19:16.
SAMIN-DURR:19:3/r3.anchor: والثالث: أنه بدل من " زكريا " بدل اشتمال لأن الوقت مشتمل عليه وسيأتي مثل هذا عند قوله

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The prophets in Adam’s, Noah’s, and Abraham’s lines preached monotheism, prayer, and zakāh, but their followers turned to polytheism, abandoned the rites, and followed innovations and desires.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: all celebrated prophets born in the progeny of Adam (sws), Noah (sws) and Abraham (sws) preached monotheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet is urged to persevere against their hostility and is given glad tidings of success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the Prophet (sws) is urged to show perseverance on their attitude and given glad tidings of success.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The adversaries mistake worldly success for proof of their truth; it is only respite until the truth is conclusively conveyed and they have no excuse when seized.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they regard their worldly successes in contrast to the believers to be a reason of their own veracity.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Jesus and Mary are prominent because Christians and Jews secretly supported Quraysh; the Qur’an exposes the People of the Book to show they cannot support a truthless cause.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the Christians too had begun to secretly support the Quraysh.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Zacharias story introduces Mary’s story and counters Christians who treat Jesus’s miraculous birth as proof of his divinity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This incident forms a prelude to the anecdote of Mary (sws) mentioned subsequently.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Zacharias probably made the prayer while in iʿtikāf at the Temple; private prayer is the foremost etiquette and aids acceptance because it is free of pretension.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: supplicating in private is its foremost etitquette and the best recommendation for its acceptance too.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan like the previous one; Muqatil exempts the prostration verse, saying it was revealed in Medina after the migration to Abyssinia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية كالسورة التي قبلها. وقال مقاتل: إلا آية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.claim: The surahs connect through astonishing stories: the earlier tells of the Cave, Moses and Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn; this one of John’s birth to an old man and barren woman and Jesus’ birth without a father.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها أنه تعالى ضمن السورة قبلها قصصا عجبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p238/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p238/r11.speaker: الحوفي وأبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p238/r11.claim: They differ on the governor of idh: al-Ḥawfī makes it dependent on dhikr, while Abū al-Baqāʾ allows raḥma or dhikr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p238/r11.anchor: وإذ ظرف العامل فيه قال الحوفي: ذكر وقال أبو البقاء: وإذ ظرف لرحمة أو لذكر

BURHAN:v2p87/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p87/r3.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v2p87/r3.claim: Al-Suhayli says nafs denotes the reality of existence without an additional sense; its relation to نفاسة and نفيس makes it suitable as a direct expression for God, unlike metaphorical terms discussed earlier.
BURHAN:v2p87/r3.anchor: وأما النفس فعبارة عن حقيقة الوجود دون معنى زائد وقد استعمل من لفظها النفاسة

BURHAN:v2p87/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p87/r4.speaker: أكثر الناس
BURHAN:v2p87/r4.claim: Most people equate ذات with nafs, essence, and existence, and cite the report about Abraham’s three statements being في ذات الله as support.
BURHAN:v2p87/r4.anchor: ويقولون ذات البارئ هي نفسه ويعبرون بها عن وجوده وحقيقته

BURHAN:v2p87/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p87/r5.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v2p87/r5.claim: Al-Suhayli rejects ذات as an expression for God’s essence: Arabic and religious usage instead mean His religion or law, as the phrase في ذات الله indicates.
BURHAN:v2p87/r5.anchor: وليست هذه اللفظة إذا استقريتها في اللغة والشريعة كما زعموا

BURHAN:v2p293/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p293/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p293/r1.claim: In Noah’s story, نادى means that he was on the verge of calling; the following explanatory فـ would be absent if the call had already occurred. Zechariah’s قال directly explains his completed call without فـ.
BURHAN:v2p293/r1.anchor: المراد قارب النداء لا أوقع النداء لدخول الفاء في فقال فإنه لو وقع النداء لسقطت

ITQAN:v4p312/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p312/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p312/r1.claim: The opponents’ failure to attempt a Qur’anic rival despite choosing warfare, captivity, and loss of property is evidence that they could not match it; an attempt would have been easier if they had the ability.
ITQAN:v4p312/r1.anchor: ولم ينقل عن أحد منهم أنه حدث نفسه بشيء من ذلك ولا رامه بل عدلوا إلى العناد تارة وإلى الإستهزاء أخرى

ITQAN:v4p312/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p312/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p312/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira called the Qur’an sweet, splendid, fruitful, and overpowering, but after Abu Jahl pressed him he called it transmitted sorcery.
ITQAN:v4p312/r2.anchor: أخرج الحاكم عن ابن عباس قال جاء الوليد بن المغيرة إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأ عليه القرآن فكأنه رق له

ITQAN:v4p312/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p312/r3.speaker: الجاحظ
ITQAN:v4p312/r3.claim: Al-Jahiz argues that Muhammad challenged Arabs at their peak in poetry, oratory, language, and numbers to produce even one sūra; their resort to accusations rather than imitation exposed their incapacity.
ITQAN:v4p312/r3.anchor: قال الجاحظ بعث الله محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم أكثر ما كانت العرب شاعرا وخطيبا وأحكم ما كانت لغة وأشد ما كانت عدة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r1.claim: A polished simile between distant kinds delights through both their strong difference and a hidden likeness that appears only after examining the relevant feature.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r1.anchor: إلا أنه كان خفيا لا ينجلى إلا بعد التألق في استحضار الصور وتذكرها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r2.claim: Ibn al-Mu'tazz likens lightning's opening and closing movement to a reader opening and closing a Quran, selecting movement while ignoring the objects' other qualities.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r2.anchor: وكأن البرق مصحف قار فانطباقا مرة وانفتاحا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r3.claim: In the reported exchange, Jarir first pities Adi ibn al-Riqa's simile of a bird to a needle, then envies him when its completion compares it to a pen drawing ink from an inkwell.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r3.anchor: في حديث عدي بن الرقاع قال جرير أنشدني عدي عرف الديار توهما فاعتادها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r4.claim: Jarir's reaction changes because the completed simile finds the nearest fitting quality in a seemingly remote object, uncovering a hidden relation.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r4.anchor: قد ظفر بأقرب صفة من أبعد موصوف وعثر على خبىء مكانه غير معروف

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r5.speaker: الخليل
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r5.claim: Jurjani next points to al-Khalil's simile concerning the contraction of a miser's hand as another example of this effect.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p131/r5.anchor: استحسنوا قول الخليل في انقباض كف البخيل

DAMGHANI:v1p157/r18.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r18.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r18.claim: Khafiya means concealed or secret; the other examples describe hidden supplication, what is secret, and what has not yet come to be.
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r18.anchor: فوجه منهما : خفي بمعنى أسر قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r1.claim: Nidāʾ is calling an addressee who is at a distance; the text lists five vocative forms: yā, ayā, hayā, ayy, and the interrogative alif.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r1.anchor: النداء : استدعاء المخاطب المخاطب إذا كان بعيدا منه - وحروف النداء خمسة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r2.claim: Poetic examples witness the vocative forms ayā, hayā, ayy, and interrogative alif; Dhū al-Rummah is named for hayā and Sībawayh for alif.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r4.claim: A second sense is supplication, illustrated by Zachariah’s quiet call and Noah’s and Job’s calls to their Lord.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r9.claim: Some add a seventh sense for nidāʾ: revelation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r9.anchor: وقد ألحق بعضهم وجها سابعا فقال : والنداء : الوحي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p791/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p791/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p791/r3.claim: Maryam’s night framing suits the hidden prayer: the secrecy of the whisper evokes the concealment of night.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p791/r3.anchor: النداء الخفي يذكّر بالليل لأن خفاء النداء يوحي بخفاء الليل فهناك تناسب بين الخفاء والليل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r1.claim: Khafiyah derives from concealment, while khīfah derives from fear; the latter appears in 7:205, unlike the خفية of 7:55 and 19:3.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r1.anchor: في اللغة الخفية: من الخفاء (إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا) والخيفة من الخوف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r5.claim: In Arabic, ḥaḍara means being present or existing, the opposite of absence, and does not necessarily mean coming to a place.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p612/r5.anchor: فعل حضر والحضور في اللغة أولاً يعني الوجود وليس معناه بالضرورة المجيء إلى الشيء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r1.claim: A text with one exclusive meaning is clear and decisive: God's intent is known from its plain wording, with no ambiguity in its ruling or interpretation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r1.anchor: معنى واحد لا يتعداه ، ومقصورا عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r2.claim: A second class of wording can bear two or more meanings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r2.anchor: أن يكون اللفظ محتملا لمعنيين أو أكثر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r3.claim: When one possible sense is plain and another hidden, take the plain sense unless evidence shows it is not intended, in which case use the hidden sense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r3.anchor: فيكون محمولا على الظاهر الجلي دون الباطن الخفي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r4.claim: If a word has a linguistic and a legal sense, prefer the legal sense because the law has transferred its meaning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r4.anchor: أحد المعنيين مستعملا في اللغة ، والآخر مستعملا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r5.claim: If a word has linguistic and customary senses, prefer the customary sense because it is the more familiar usage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r5.anchor: أحد المعنيين مستعملا في اللغة ، والآخر مستعملا في العرف

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r6.claim: If a word has legal and customary senses, prefer the legal sense because the law is more binding.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r6.anchor: مستعملا في الشرع ، والآخر مستعملا في العرف ، فيكون

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r7.claim: Even when two senses share the same basis, they may be used equally in language, law, or custom; the case then divides further.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r7.anchor: في اللغة على سواء ، أو في الشرع ، أو في العرف

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r8.claim: Where same-basis senses conflict and cannot be combined, as with quruʾ meaning either purity or menstruation, a jurist must infer which is intended from the indicators.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r8.anchor: مثل القرء الذي هو حقيقة في الطهر ، وحقيقة في الحيض

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r9.claim: Each mujtahid's conclusion from the indicators is God's intended meaning for that jurist, even when another jurist's effort reaches the opposite ruling.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p38/r9.anchor: كان هو الذي أراده الله تعالى منه ، وإن أدى اجتهاد غيره
